source_snapshot.procedure: Labels a Fatal action and gives split railtype10/voltagetype0/dimm0 lines for every DIMM and voltage types0/1.
source_snapshot.criteria: Calls the event correctable and requires tool PASS and OS reporting.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic current logs do not prove measured warning current, duration or avoidance of limiter/trip.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds monitoring but lacks severity reconciliation, selector semantics, calibrated thresholds, hysteresis and safe-current acceptance.

old_problem: Fatal versus correctable-warning semantics conflict; railtype10/voltage parameters, sensor and PMIC/I2C targets, warning/limiter/trip thresholds, duration/hysteresis, reset behavior and recovery are not authoritative.
disposition_reason: A current-warning test must stay below limiter, trip and component limits. Those thresholds and stimulus semantics are safety-critical rather than runtime bindings; ED-12/15/16/18 therefore keep execution Pending/BLOCKED until calibrated limits, an approved stimulus and restoration exist.
decision_basis: Read exact row98/history2496 and kept warning coverage separate from row97 PGOOD and row99 current-limiter behavior.
Preserved railtype10, dual voltage parameters, every DIMM, fatal label, correctable criterion and OS evidence.
Required calibrated current plus rail/thermal/fan observation and explicit warning-versus-limiter status.
Required a documented clear/deassertion and memory recovery between targets.
No threshold, sensor, tuple or timeout was guessed and no DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: DDR5 PMIC high-current consumption warning transition
test_case.purpose: For each approved PMIC/current sensor, inject one bounded high-current warning condition, prove a correctable warning without reaching limiter/trip or causing reset, thermal or memory damage, then clear and restore baseline.
required_package: Approved severity/reset policy plus warning, limiter and trip bands
Duration, hysteresis, latch/clear and electrical/thermal abort limits
Complete command matrix, source-specific event oracle and recovery
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the ambiguous source tuple or create uncontrolled load. Once approved, baseline calibrated current, voltage, temperature, fans, raw status and memory; apply one exact bounded synthetic/vendor stimulus; capture the warning transition and absence of limiter/trip; clear by the approved method and restore state before another target.
test_case.expected_result: Measured current enters only the signed warning band for the authorized duration, the target warning asserts once with no limiter/trip/unapproved reset, rails and temperatures remain safe, and after clear current, status, fans, DIMMs, memory and configuration return to baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires calibrated warning-band evidence, exact target/status, protection-boundary margin and complete clear/recovery. Generic logs, guessed current, limiter/trip, unsafe droop/temperature, reset, DIMM/MCA error or stale status fails.
safety_gate: Instrumented isolated SUT with independent OOB and calibrated current/voltage/thermal capture.
One approved PMIC/parameter once below limiter/trip/component limits.
Abort on overcurrent, droop, overheating, limiter/trip, unapproved reset, I2C loss or memory error.
No automatic load, clear, retry or traversal.
expected_evidence: Exact tuple and synchronized current-warning timeline
Fresh PMIC/CPER/SEL warning with zero limiter/trip/reset delta
Approved clear, stable rails/thermal/fans, full DIMM/memory and restoration diff
test_case.recovery: Remove only the approved stimulus, preserve evidence, clear the warning through the signed method, and restore PMIC recovery, SPD/telemetry, I2C and BIOS/HDT. Verify normal current/rails/temperature/fans and all memory; do not retry a protection event.

source_conflict.reason: Fatal/correctable-warning conflict, fixed tuple population and missing selector, threshold, hysteresis and protection-boundary semantics remain unresolved.

blocked.reason: An undefined current stimulus can cross limiter/trip limits, overheat power delivery, reset the host or corrupt memory.
